items.title: Georg Brunis Interview, 1958-06-03
items.q: We had Abby, Merritt, and Richie on trumpets, and my brother Henry on the trombone, and I played the upright alto.

ctx.x: And Rudy was the oldest in the family.

Yeah. And he was a brewmeister. No, Richie's after, before. And Rudy was a brewmeister in the New Orleans Brewing Company. And then there was Henry, then there was Merritt, and there's Albert and myself, and my brother Richard, the four of us are living here. And my sister and my mother, they played guitar, both guitar and piano. And my old man would get us out after dinner and make us all. We had Abby, Merritt, and Richie on trumpets, and my brother Henry on the trombone, and I played the upright alto. I was…

items.title: Brunies Brother Band Interview, 1957-10-19
items.q: So Georgie, when I laid the trombone down, Georgie picked it up.

ctx.x: . Now we have some time. Yeah, it's going all right now. If you can just tell us first, forget your name on Abby, so we know. Okay, this is Abby Brunus speaking. And now these folks are here wanting to know how I started. It's been so long, it's hard to remember. We're back there in 1908. When were you born? In 1900. And we started out, I think we were the first school band in the United States. There was only three pieces. And the three pieces consist of Emmett Rogers, George Brunus, and myself. And then we...…

You say Henry could read a good reader, but the rest of you never did learn to read. No, none of us read outside of Henry. Henry would sit down and play first chair in a big 60-piece band.
